================================================================================
                      THE SHIP — OFFICIAL SYSTEM MANUAL & API
================================================================================

Welcome Commander! This manual contains the complete technical reference for
controlling all ship subsystems, flight controls, trading, telemetry, dashboard
widgets, and Kubernetes vendor management.

Base Host: 192.168.103.40 (Accessible via WireGuard VPN)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. TELEMETRY & SENSORS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Query your ship's real-time position, heading angle, and velocity vector.

* Sensor Endpoint (Port 2011 / 2010):
  $ curl http://192.168.103.40:2011/pos
  Response:
  {
    "kind": "success",
    "pos": { "x": 100.0, "y": 250.0, "angle": 45.0 },
    "velocity": { "x": 1.2, "y": 3.4, "angle": 0.0 }
  }

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. NAVIGATION & AUTOPILOT (Port 2009)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Set flight targets using station names, raw coordinates, or control states.

* Fly to a Named Station:
  $ curl -XPOST http://192.168.103.40:2009/set_target -d '{"target": "Core Station"}'
  $ curl -XPOST http://192.168.103.40:2009/set_target -d '{"target": "Azura Station"}'
  $ curl -XPOST http://192.168.103.40:2009/set_target -d '{"target": "Vesta Station"}'

* Fly to Exact Coordinates (x, y):
  $ curl -XPOST http://192.168.103.40:2009/set_target -d '{"target": {"x": 7000, "y": 7000}}'

* Autopilot Modes:
  $ curl -XPOST http://192.168.103.40:2009/set_target -d '{"target": "stop"}'   # Emergency brake
  $ curl -XPOST http://192.168.103.40:2009/set_target -d '{"target": "idle"}'   # Drift mode

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. MANUAL THRUSTERS & PROPULSION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Direct individual control of ship thrusters (0% to 100% power).

* Thruster Port Mapping:
  - Port 2003: Main Engine / Thruster 1
  - Port 2004: Port Thruster / Thruster 2
  - Port 2006: Starboard Thruster / Thruster 3
  - Port 2007: Maneuvering Thruster / Thruster 4
  - Port 2008: Braking Thruster / Thruster 5

* Setting Thrust:
  $ curl -XPUT http://192.168.103.40:2003/thruster -d '{"thrust_percent": 100}'
  $ curl -XPUT http://192.168.103.40:2003/thruster -d '{"thrust_percent": 0}'

* Reading Thruster State:
  $ curl http://192.168.103.40:2003/thruster
  Response: {"kind": "success", "thrust_percent": 100}

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. CARGO HOLD & ECONOMY (Port 2012)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Inspect your current cargo inventory, credit balance, and hold capacity.

* Cargo Status:
  $ curl http://192.168.103.40:2012/hold
  Response:
  {
    "kind": "success",
    "hold": {
      "resources": { "IRON": 10, "GOLD": 0 },
      "credits": 550,
      "hold_size": 40,
      "hold_free": 30
    }
  }

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. COMMERCE & TRADING (Port 2011)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Trade resources with nearby stations.

* Check Stations in Reach:
  $ curl http://192.168.103.40:2011/stations_in_reach
  Response:
  {
    "kind": "success",
    "stations": {
      "Core Station": {
        "resources": { "IRON": { "buy_price": 50, "sell_price": 40 } }
      }
    }
  }

* Buy Resources:
  $ curl -XPOST http://192.168.103.40:2011/buy -d '{"station": "Azura Station", "what": "IRON", "amount": 5}'

* Sell Resources:
  $ curl -XPOST http://192.168.103.40:2011/sell -d '{"station": "Core Station", "what": "IRON", "amount": 5}'

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. LIVE DASHBOARD & CUSTOM WIDGETS (Port 2002)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Your personal web dashboard communicates over a raw TCP socket on Port 2002.
Messages are JSON objects terminated by a null-byte (\0).

* Protocol Messages:
  1. 'update_widget': Registers or updates a widget on your live web UI.
  2. 'update_doc': Updates the documentation tab in your web interface.
  3. 'keepalive': Sent in response to null bytes to maintain socket connection.

* Example Widget Message:
  {
    "kind": "update_widget",
    "widget": {
      "title": "Ship Navigation",
      "group": "navigation",
      "width": 2,
      "height": 2,
      "content": {
        "kind": "text",
        "text": "Current Target: Vesta Station\nPosition: (7000, 7000)"
      }
    }
  }

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. KUBERNETES VENDOR MANAGEMENT (Port 6443)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The ship backend resources are orchestrated under the 'theship-vendor' namespace.

* View All Deployed Pods & Services:
  $ kubectl --kubeconfig=~/.kube/config get all -n theship-vendor

* ~/.kube/config:
apiVersion: v1
clusters:
- cluster:
    certificate-authority-data: 
    server: https://192.168.103.40:6443
  name: default
contexts:
- context:
    cluster: default
    user: default
  name: default
current-context: default
kind: Config
preferences: {}
users:
- name: default
  user:
    client-certificate-data: 
    client-key-data:
